main_text.p: Gens, hypocritae, impij nebulones in populo Iudaico, Pfal.43. 1. Efa.1.4. & 10.6. & 49.7.
Gens figuratè sumitur pro locuftarum numerosissimis minibus què fruges terrę vorarunt & consumpserunt, Ioel.1.6.
Gentes synecdochicè pro primis parentibus & stirpi-us duarum gentium, Gen.25.23.

Gentes, populi, vel multi, vel omnes, præter Iudæos: ex-a fœdus, incircuncisi, Gentiles: quorum magna pars ad Christi cognitionem adducta per Euangelium, familia Dei per fidem in Mediatores insita est. Gen. 10. 5. & 22. & 49. 10. Exo.30.10. Leu.1.8.24. Iud.2.21. Sam.8.20.2. Reg.16.3.2. Par.9.14. Esdr.4.10. Pfal.2.v.1.8. Efa.2.2. Ioel.2. Malach.1.11. Act.13.v.47.48. Rom.1.5. & 3.29. & 11.v.12. 25.1. Cor.1.23. Eph.2.11. Apoc.11.2. & 22.2.

GENTES: Gentes omnes in gloriam Dei creatæ, Deut.26.19. ut paulatim ejectæ e terra Chanaan, 7.22. cur ibidem re-ctæ, Iud.3.1. Gentes ignorantiæ prętextu non excusandę Rom.2.14. Gentes pro nationibus à Dei cultu & fœdere alienis, 1.Cor.12.2. vt explicatur Ephef. 2. v.11.12. Gentes Legem non habentes (quod tamen non simpliciter, sed κατὰ φύσιν est intelligendum, id est, habita Iudæorum ratione, quibus Deus singula Legis capita tradidit, Exo. 20.1.) quæ legis sunt, faciunt, Roman.2.14. hoc est, honesta iubent, turpia prohibent, & puniunt.

page.notes: The left edge shows faint text from the neighbouring page, not transcribed. Several Greek words in the paragraph beginning "GENTES: Gentes omnes" are set in Greek and are copied as printed where legible; the Greek phrase "κατὰ φύσιν" is a reading from the scan and may be imperfect. Scan is low resolution; some Latin abbreviations and numerals in the Scripture references are doubtful.
